andrew (eng-platform): Heads up — customer asked us to stop automatic spillover from Dedicated -> Hosted unless they explicitly opt in. want to align routing + console UX + telemetry.
maya (eng-sre): +1. we currently treat dedicated overflow as transparent for best-effort burst. customers have complained about data boundaries though.
sasha (eng-runtime): We have two levers: routing policy (router decision) and handshake metadata (tenant flags). If we add an opt-in flag it should be honored by the runtime and the broker.
oliver (product): Important: discoverability in console. We need a single toggle that makes clear consequences (latency, cost, data plane). UX copy matters.
kevin (support): Saw one support ticket where a customer was charged hosted rates after spillover. They didn't realize it happened. we should emit an audit event and a user-facing notification.
andrew (eng-platform): Agree. Proposal:
1) new tenant setting `allow_hosted_fallback` default false
2) router will only route to hosted if tenant.allow_hosted_fallback == true
3) console: toggle + CTA linking to billing/terms
4) telemetry: emit `fallback_decision` with fields {tenant, from_pool, to_pool, reason, model_variant}
5) rollout: start with internal tenants and a few opt-in customers
sasha (eng-runtime): Sample policy snippet i sketched:
```
{"routing": {"preferred_pool": "dedicated", "fallback": ["same-region-dedicated", "hosted"], "fallback_policy": {"hosted": {"require_flag": "allow_hosted_fallback"}}}}
```
maya (eng-sre): Nice. For telemetry we should also track token counts served on fallback and peak qps when fallback occurred. That helps billing reconciliation.
kevin (support): Also add an explanation copy for invoices — "Requests served on hosted after capacity overflow" or similar.
oliver (product): UX question: if a tenant toggles the flag on, do we show a persistent banner: "Your requests may be served on hosted infra"? I'd prefer affirmative consent and a one-time modal.
andrew (eng-platform): Modal + audit event sounds good. We also need API counterpart: PATCH /tenants/:id with allow_hosted_fallback true/false. Should be admin-only.
sasha (eng-runtime): Implementation note: runtime needs to annotate response header `x-fallback-used: hosted` so downstream logs and customers can see it. Also add `x-fallback-variant: gptq-xx` if model variant differs.
maya (eng-sre): Two safety concerns: 1) ensure data plane isolation — make sure hosted doesn't log tenant-id in a way that's accessible to other tenants; 2) if hosted is used for regulated tenant, block by default and add an override path with org-legal signoff.
kevin (support): We'll need a support playbook: how to explain, how to refund if wrong charges, and how to switch off quickly.
andrew (eng-platform): Rollout plan draft:
- stage 1: add tenant flag + router checks + telemetry events (internal-only)
- stage 2: console toggle behind feature flag + modal + audit events
- stage 3: public rollout + billing note
- stage 4: opt-in assistance for customers migrating from 'always spill' behavior
sasha (eng-runtime): Curious edge-case: model variant mismatch. If dedicated only has quantized variant A and hosted has fp16 B, we must include `variant_compat` check and optionally translate outputs. Prefer explicit variant selection in policy.
andrew (eng-platform): Good call. we'll add a `variant_compatibility` boolean and `allowed_variants` list to policy.
kevin (support): One more: telemetry consumers (billing team) want an aggregated daily metric `tokens_hosted_fallback_by_tenant`. add to spec.
maya (eng-sre): Ops: add alert if fallback rate > 5% of requests for a tenant over 10m window. that's a signal they're undersized or abused.
oliver (product): For console, add a small graph on tenant page: % requests served on dedicated vs hosted over last 7d. link to billing.
andrew (eng-platform): I'll open an RFC PR with the proposed API, router change, telemetry schema, console mock. tagging sasha + maya for impl.
robo-deploy: deploy-bot: new branch created: feature/fallback-optin-rfc (PR #452) :white_check_mark:
kevin (support): Thanks — i'll prep support doc draft and a short email template for customers.
sasha (eng-runtime): i'll start on runtime checks and header emission. expecting ~3 sprint work.
maya (eng-sre): i'll add telemetry + alerting rules. want to pair on schema.
andrew (eng-platform): cool. next step: review RFC. thx everyone. :thumbsup:
